How to do itPendlay Row

Start position

Right
BACK FLAT
Wrong
BACK ROUNDED

Right: Torso level, back flat, hips a little above deadlift height.

Wrong: Back rounded to reach the bar.

Top position

Right
TORSO LEVEL
Wrong
TORSO RISES

Right: Bar at chest base. Torso level, shoulders not shrugged.

Wrong: Torso risen up to yank the bar.

Keep your torso level with the floor, shoulders and hips at one height.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Back roundedThe back is rounded to reach the bar on the floor.
  2. Hips tuck underThe hips tuck under and the back curls down.
Pull1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Grip

Overhand, thumbs around the bar. Straps are fine if grip fails first.

Keep the wrists from curling forward.

Common handling mistakes

  • Starting with a rounded back

    Fix: Raise the bar on blocks or plates. Keep the back flat.

  • Standing partly up to yank

    Fix: Use less weight. Keep the torso level, hips not forward.

  • Elbows flared wide

    Fix: Lighten the load. Pull the bar toward the hips.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your upper back and sides. Hamstrings and lower back hold the position.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • FixStop the set. Don't train through the pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    New to lifting? Start with seated or chest-supported rows first.

  2. 2

    Bar on the floor. Stand over it, feet flat, shoulder width.

  3. 3

    Hips a little above deadlift height. Grip slightly wider than shoulders. Brace.

  4. 4

    Back rounds to reach it? Raise the bar on blocks or plates.

  5. 5

    Beat target by one or two reps? Add 2 to 10 percent.

Risks and when to stop

  • Starting a rep with a rounded back is dangerous.
  • Of the rows tested, the bent-over row loaded the lower spine most.
  • Heavy reps with a held breath send blood pressure very high.

Back pain

How to do itLandmine Row

Back line

Right
BACK STRAIGHT
Wrong
LOWER BACK ROUNDS

Right: Back straight, torso level, braced.

Wrong: Lower back rounded over the bar.

Keep your back straight and your torso roughly level with the floor.

  1. Lower back roundsThe lower back rounds over the bar.
  2. Hips tuck underThe hips tuck under as the back curls.
Pull1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Grip

Overhand, one hand above the other. Thumbs wrapped around the bar, not alongside it.

Keep the wrists from curling forward.

Common handling mistakes

  • Rounding the lower back

    Fix: Brace before each rep and use a lighter load.

  • Jerking it up

    Fix: Pull with control. Squeeze the shoulder blades at the top.

  • Stopping short at the bottom

    Fix: Lower until the arms are straight.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this between and around your shoulder blades.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • FixBrace first and use a lighter load.

  • FixStop the set. Don't train through the pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Anchor a barbell end in a landmine. Load the free end.

  2. 2

    Straddle the loaded end, feet between hip and shoulder width.

  3. 3

    Hinge until the torso is roughly level with the floor, back straight.

  4. 4

    Both hands overhand below the plates, one above the other.

  5. 5

    Beat target by one or two reps? Add 2 to 10 percent.

Risks and when to stop

  • A rounded back strains the lower back and raises the chance of injury.
  • Of the rows tested, the bent-over row loaded the lower spine most.
  • Heavy reps with a held breath send blood pressure very high.

How to do itOne-Arm Dumbbell Row

Top position

Right
TORSO SQUARE
Wrong
TORSO TWISTS

Right: Elbow driven back, dumbbell at the hip, torso square.

Wrong: Torso twisted open to lift higher.

Put your supporting hand under your shoulder and your knee under your hip.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Arm not straightThe arm never straightens at the bottom.
  2. Not loweredThe dumbbell never comes all the way down.
Pull2 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Grip

One dumbbell in the working hand, thumb wrapped around the handle.

Keep the wrist from curling forward.

Common handling mistakes

  • Jerking it up with momentum

    Fix: Pull slowly and lower gently.

  • Twisting to lift higher

    Fix: Stop the pull where your torso would have to turn.

  • Elbow flaring out

    Fix: Keep the elbow close to the body and drive it back.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this at the side of your back, around your shoulder blade.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansPulling toward the shoulder works the biceps more.

    FixPull toward your hip instead.

  • Usually meansYour back is usually stronger than your grip.

    FixUse a lifting strap.

  • FixStop the set. Don't train through the pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Dumbbell on the floor beside a flat bench.

  2. 2

    One knee and the same-side hand on the bench.

  3. 3

    Hand under the shoulder, not far forward. Knee under the hip.

  4. 4

    Back flat and level, eyes on the floor below you.

  5. 5

    Brace, then let the arm hang straight, shoulder not dropping.

Risks and when to stop

  • The shoulder is a common injury site in weight training. Poor technique adds risk.

Shoulder pain

How to do itDumbbell Romanian Deadlift

Bottom position

Right
FLAT BACK
Wrong
BACK ROUNDS

Right: Hips back, flat back, soft knees, dumbbells at mid-shin.

Wrong: Rounded back, reaching the dumbbells lower.

Push your hips back, not down, and keep your knees softly bent.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Back archesThe lower back arches to stand up.
  2. Hips stay backThe hips stay back while the back does the lifting.
Lower2 s
Stand1 s
Look closer

Grip

Dumbbells on the thighs, palms facing you, thumbs wrapped.

Keep the wrist neutral, in line with the forearm.

Common handling mistakes

  • Arching to stand up

    Fix: Push through the heels with glutes and hamstrings. Back neutral.

  • Rounding to reach lower

    Fix: Stop where the back stays flat. If it rounds, go lighter.

  • Going too low

    Fix: Stop where the hamstrings stop the hinge.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the backs of your thighs going down, glutes coming up.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • FixPush the hips back and keep only a slight knee bend.

  • FixUse your glutes and hamstrings to stand up.

  • FixStop the set. Don't train through the pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Feet shoulder width. Dumbbells on thighs, not hanging away from the legs.

  2. 2

    Shoulder blades down and back. Breathe in and brace before each rep.

  3. 3

    Knees behind the toes. Eyes to the floor as you lower.

  4. 4

    Want more range? Stand on a plate.

  5. 5

    Add weight in small steps once you beat your target reps.

Risks and when to stop

  • Rounding the back to reach lower raises injury risk.
  • Heavy reps with a held breath send blood pressure very high.
  • Looking straight ahead at the bottom strains the neck.

How to do itConventional Deadlift

Start position

Right
FLAT BACK
Wrong
BACK ROUNDS

Right: Bar over mid-foot, shins near it, arms straight, back flat.

Wrong: Lower back rounds as the bar leaves the floor.

Liftoff

Right
HIPS WAIT
Wrong
HIPS SHOOT UP

Right: Legs start the pull, hips wait for the bar.

Wrong: Hips shoot up before the bar moves.

Start with the bar over the middle of your foot, shins close.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Lower back roundsThe lower back rounds as the bar leaves the floor.
  2. Hips tuck underThe hips tuck under and the back curls over the bar.
Lift1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Grip

Overhand, thumbs wrapped, hands about shoulder width, outside the knees. Use mixed grip or straps only when grip limits heavy sets.

Keep the wrist neutral, in line with the forearm.

Common handling mistakes

  • Back rounding under heavier weight

    Fix: Lower the weight or do fewer reps per set.

  • Hips shooting up first

    Fix: Be patient off the floor so the legs start the pull.

  • Hands too wide, arms bent

    Fix: Grip about shoulder width. Straighten the arms before pulling.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your glutes and hamstrings, not your back. Front thighs help off the floor.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • FixLower the weight or do fewer reps.

  • FixStop the set. Don't train through the pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Load the bar on the floor with full-size plates.

  2. 2

    Bar over mid-foot, feet hip to shoulder width, toes slightly out.

  3. 3

    Breathe in and brace. Build tension slowly before liftoff.

  4. 4

    Finish tall: hips and knees locked, shoulders back.

  5. 5

    To lower, push hips back first. Bend knees once the bar passes.

Risks and when to stop

  • A rounded back loads the spine's discs and bones more.
  • Heavy reps with a held breath send blood pressure very high.
  • Big load jumps appear linked with more injuries. Add weight in small steps.

Back pain

How to do itSumo Deadlift

Start position

Right
CHEST UP
Wrong
HIPS SHOOT UP

Right: Chest up, trunk upright, bar on shins, back flat.

Wrong: Hips shoot up while the bar stays on the floor.

Keep the bar against your shins so it does not drift forward.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Hips shoot upThe hips rise first while the bar stays on the floor.
  2. Chest dropsThe chest drops toward the bar and the back takes the lift.
Lift1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Grip

Overhand, thumbs wrapped, hands inside the knees.

Keep the wrist neutral, in line with the forearm.

Common handling mistakes

  • Hips shooting up first

    Fix: Be patient and keep driving with the legs.

  • Rushing the setup

    Fix: Set feet, grip and brace before each pull.

  • Bar drifting off the shins

    Fix: Chest up and keep the bar against the shins.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your glutes, inner and front thighs, most off the floor.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • FixStay patient and keep driving with the legs.

  • FixStop the set. Don't train through the pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Wide stance, toes out, bar over mid-foot, shins vertical from the front.

  2. 2

    Arms inside the knees, not outside as in a conventional pull.

  3. 3

    Lock knees and hips out together. Lower the bar with control.

  4. 4

    Build tension, then take a full breath into the belly.

  5. 5

    Practise with light weight. Add load in small steps.

Risks and when to stop

  • Sumo loads the lower back a little less, but heavier weight can offset that.
  • Heavy reps with a held breath send blood pressure very high.
  • Hips rising first shifts the lift onto the back.

How to do itBack Extension

Pad height

Right
HIPS HINGE
Wrong
BACK CURLS

Right: Pad on the upper thighs, below the hip bones.

Wrong: Pad too high, back curled over it.

Right
STRAIGHT LINE

Right: Shoulders, spine and hips in one line. Squeeze the glutes.

Set the pad on your upper thighs, below your hip bones.

Tells
  1. Back roundsThe back rounds over the pad.
  2. Hips stay stiffThe hips barely hinge, so the spine bends instead.
Lower2 s
Raise1 s
Hold1 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your glutes, hamstrings and lower back. A pump, not a deep ache.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansDoing too much too soon can hurt your back.

    FixTake a week or two off, then come back lighter and check your form.

  • FixStop the set. Don't train through the pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Pad on the top of your thighs, just below the hip bones.

  2. 2

    Feet about shoulder width and secured, knees slightly bent.

  3. 3

    Cross your arms over your chest (hands behind the head is harder).

  4. 4

    Lower to just below parallel. Breathe in, then out as you rise.

  5. 5

    Start with body weight. Add weight after 12 to 15 good reps.

Risks and when to stop

  • Doing too much too soon can hurt the back.
  • Swinging with momentum raises injury risk.
  • Rounding the back is more dangerous with added weight.

How to do itT-Bar Row

Back line

Right
BACK STRAIGHT
Wrong
BACK ROUNDS

Right: Back straight, chest level with the floor, soft knees.

Wrong: Back rounded over the bar.

Keep your back straight and your chest level with the floor.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Back roundsThe back rounds forward over the bar.
  2. Hips tuck underThe hips tuck under as the back curls.
Pull1 s
Hold1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Grip

Palms facing, thumbs wrapped around the V-handle, not alongside it. Straps are fine on heavy sets.

Keep the wrists from curling forward.

Common handling mistakes

  • Rounding the back

    Fix: Brace and use a lighter load.

  • Swinging the weight up

    Fix: Pull the shoulder blades back. Hold the squeeze at the top.

  • Stopping halfway down

    Fix: Lower all the way, slowly, each rep.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the middle and sides of your back. Your lower back works hard too.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • FixStop the set. Don't train through the pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Barbell in a landmine, plates on the free end.

  2. 2

    Hook a V-handle under the bar about 8-10 inches from the plates.

  3. 3

    Stand over the bar, feet about shoulder width, knees slightly bent.

  4. 4

    Hinge, chest level with the floor. Grab the handle, palms facing.

  5. 5

    Beat target by one or two reps? Add 2 to 10 percent.

Risks and when to stop

  • A rounded back strains the lower back and raises the chance of injury.
  • Without a chest pad the lower back works much harder.
  • Heavy reps with a held breath send blood pressure very high.

Top position

Right
ARMS STRAIGHT
Wrong
ELBOWS BENT

Right: Shoulders up toward the ears, arms straight.

Wrong: Elbows bent, pulling the bar up with the arms.

Keep your elbows straight and let your arms just hang.

Lift1 s

Grip

Overhand, hands about shoulder width, thumbs wrapped around the bar.

Common handling mistakes

  • Rolling the shoulders

    Fix: Lift straight up, lower straight down.

  • Bending the arms to pull

    Fix: Keep your elbows straight. If you can't, lower the weight.

  • Dropping the bar fast

    Fix: Lower slowly to the start.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this on top of your shoulders, between neck and shoulder.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

Set it up

  1. 1

    Overhand grip, hands about shoulder width, thumbs around the bar.

  2. 2

    Stand tall with knees slightly bent and hips straight.

  3. 3

    Let the bar hang in front of your thighs on straight arms.

  4. 4

    Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears. No rolling.

  5. 5

    Beat target by one or two reps? Add 2 to 10 percent.

Risks and when to stop

  • Heavy reps with a held breath send blood pressure very high.
  • The shoulder is a common injury site in lifting. Poor technique adds risk.

Grip

Common handling mistakes

  • Not standing up straight

  4. 4

    Stand up straight, head up, eyes forward.

    Beat target by one or two reps? Add 2 to 10 percent.

  • Heavy reps with a held breath send blood pressure very high.
  • The shoulder is a common injury site in weight training. Poor technique adds risk.
